# CV files (`cvs/*.cv.json`)

One JSON document per CV, `"format": "enginecv.authoring/v1"`. Schema: https://enginecv.app/schema/authoring/v1.json. Keep `format` and `id` as they are.

## Fields

- format: "enginecv.authoring/v1" (required)
- design (optional hints): template, accent ("#rrggbb"), cvLanguage
- basics: name, headline, email, phone, location, website, linkedin, github, links, drivingLicense, nationality, dateOfBirth, passport, nationalId, maritalStatus, militaryService, genderPronoun, disability, visa, height
- summary: Markdown text
- experience[]: position, company, location, start, end, description, highlights, skills, url
- education[]: institution, studyType, area, location, start, end, score, description, courses, skills, url
- courses[]: name, institution, location, start, end, description, skills, url
- projects[]: name, subtitle, start, end, description, highlights, keywords, skills, url, repos, visibility
- organisations[]: name, role, location, start, end, description, skills, url
- certificates[]: name, issuer, date, description, skills, url, issuerUrl
- awards[]: name, issuer, date, description, skills, url
- publications[]: name, publisher, date, description, skills, url
- references[]: name, position, organisation, email, phone, description, url
- declaration: text, fullName, place, date
- skills: ["name", ...] or { "Group": ["name", { "name", "level" }] }; level: beginner, amateur, competent, proficient, expert
- languages: ["Language: level", ...]; level: A1–C2 or native
- interests: ["name", ...] or [{ name, description }]
- custom[]: { title, text } or { title, tags: [...] } or { title, entries: [{ title, subtitle, location, start, end, description, skills, url }] }

## Entries

- Dates are "YYYY" or "YYYY-MM"; an end date still running is "present". Leave a date out when unknown.
- Text fields are Markdown (bold, italic, links, bullet lists).
- Every entry may carry `id`. Keep it when you edit the entry; leave it out for a new entry and EngineCV assigns one.
- `"hidden": true` keeps an entry out of the printed CV.

## Edit safely

- Change only the value you were asked about. Add an entry by appending an object to the section's array. Remove an entry only when asked.
- Never invent facts, employers, dates, numbers or skills. Keep the person's wording and language.
- Save the whole file in one write, valid JSON (double quotes, no comments, no trailing commas).
- If the new file would keep fewer than half of a CV's entries and drop three or more, EngineCV holds it for the person to review instead of applying it.
- Harmless slips (a code fence, a trailing comma, a byte-order mark) are repaired with a notice. A cut-off or invalid file is refused and the CV stays as it was; read `.enginecv/results/`.
- Sign your work: add a top-level `"edited_by": "<your name>"` (for example `Claude Code`). EngineCV shows it in a notification so the person sees what changed and who did it.
- Keys EngineCV does not know are ignored with a notice.

## Not in the file

Design (template, colours, fonts), the photo and the signature belong to the app. Do not add them.

If the person left contact details out of the files, `basics` has no email, phone or links. Do not add them.
